C08-M04-L04-F1.title: One outbound connection through source NAT
C08-M04-L04-F1.caption: How fw01 rewrites a workstation's connection to its public address, reverses the translation for replies, and records both identities in its session log.
C08-M04-L04-F1.alt: Sequence diagram with four lanes: Workstation WS-104 (10.40.0.23), Firewall fw01 (SNAT to 203.0.113.10), Web server (198.51.100.80) and SIEM. The workstation sends SYN 10.40.0.23:51290 to 198.51.100.80:443 to the firewall. The firewall sends SYN from 203.0.113.10:40112 (after SNAT) to the web server. The web server replies, dashed, SYN/ACK to 203.0.113.10:40112. The firewall replies, dashed, SYN/ACK to 10.40.0.23:51290 (reversed). The workstation sends data, then FIN: session closes. The firewall sends the session-end log with src, nat_src, bytes and duration to the SIEM.

messages.label: Session-end log: src, nat_src, bytes, duration

C08-M04-L04-F1.note: Outside, every Banyan host is 203.0.113.10; only the firewall's session log links a public port back to an internal host.

C08-M04-L04-F2.title: Connection patterns in firewall logs and their look-alikes
C08-M04-L04-F2.caption: Six connection patterns an analyst recognises in firewall logs, the log signature of each and the benign activity that produces the same shape.
C08-M04-L04-F2.alt: Table with columns Pattern, Log signature and Benign look-alike. Vertical port scan: one SRC, one DST, many DPT, seconds; authorised vulnerability scan. Horizontal sweep: one SRC, one DPT, many DST; internet background scanning. Outbound to blocked port: internal SRC, DPT 445 or 25, denied, repeated; misconfigured app or roaming laptop. Regular small sessions: same DST, fixed interval, similar bytes; update checks, telemetry, NTP. Large outbound bytes: bytes out far above bytes in, rare DST; backup, cloud sync, video call. Out-of-state deny: ACK or PSH without SYN, dropped; idle timeout, asymmetric routing.
